_note: Scored experiments are families of workload instances drawn from the paper's own evaluation settings (Sections 4.2-4.3). Each method is run as a solver on every instance under the paper's 120 s solver limit; train instances are public (eval/train/instances.json), test instances are held out. The family means are not quantities the paper reports, so the paper's numbers are kept under '_' keys (per experiment and in '_paper_reported') rather than as results the gym must match. Setup scaling: 6 instances per family per slice instead of the paper's full sweeps; otherwise node counts, optical degrees, bandwidths (800/k Gbps), base latency (20 us) and switching latencies follow the paper.

allreduce_scaling.description: Paper Fig. 8(a) setting: Rabenseifner AllReduce on 64-1024 nodes, k=4 optical planes at 200 Gbps, 16-64 MB payloads, 20 us base latency, 200 us reconfiguration latency.

cct_reduction_vs_strawman_pct.description: Mean over the family's instances of the percent full-collective completion-time reduction versus the lockstep Strawman-ICR schedule computed by the evaluator (per instance clipped to [-100, 100]). A failed run scores -100.

valid_schedule.description: 1 if every instance of every experiment got a physically valid schedule within the time limit (traffic conservation, plane indices < k, alpha-beta transmission time, switching latency, per-plane serial use, step barriers); 0 for a failed run.

allreduce_scaling._paper_note: Anchor: the paper's Fig. 8(a) reduction over Strawman-ICR at 64 nodes (32 MB, k=4), 39.6%, growing to 46.9% at 512 nodes. The scored value is a mean over 64-1024 nodes and 16-64 MB payloads, which the paper does not report; the anchor is a paper point, not a target.

collective_algorithms.description: Paper Fig. 7 setting: Rabenseifner ReduceScatter and AllReduce, Bruck All-to-All (128-512 nodes) and Pairwise All-to-All (9-12 nodes) on k=8 optical planes at 100 Gbps, 1-512 MB payloads, 200 us reconfiguration latency.

cct_reduction_vs_strawman_pct.description: Mean over the family's instances of the percent full-collective completion-time reduction versus the lockstep Strawman-ICR schedule computed by the evaluator (per instance clipped to [-100, 100]). A failed run scores -100.

collective_algorithms._paper_note: Anchor: the paper's Fig. 7(b) peak ('up to') AllReduce reduction over Strawman-ICR, 87.1% (256 nodes, k=8, B=100 Gbps); other algorithms' peaks under '_paper_fig7_peak_*'. Peaks over a message-size sweep, not means: the scored family mean over 1-512 MB is expected to be lower. Not a target.

hardware_sensitivity.description: Paper Section 4.3 setting: 256-node Rabenseifner/Bruck (9 or 17 node Pairwise) collectives with optical degree k in {2,4,8} at 800/k Gbps and reconfiguration latency in {0.02, 0.2, 2, 20} ms, 1-256 MB payloads.

hardware_sensitivity._paper_note: Section 4.3 reports robustness only graphically (Figs. 10-11), noting that at k=8 the 120 s solver limit can give sub-optimal schedules. Anchor: the paper's only numeric k=2 result, the Fig. 5 example (1500 -> 1200 us, 20%). The scored family (k in {2,4,8}, 0.02-20 ms switching) is not on that scale; not a target.

_paper_reported._note: The paper's reported numbers, unchanged from earlier iterations. The three named instances are reproduced as unscored experiments in scoring/scores.json.

_weights_note: Weights 0.4/0.4/0.2 (iteration 11): the paper's headline quantitative claims are algorithm-level efficiency (Fig. 7) and cluster scalability (Fig. 8); Section 4.3 robustness is reported only graphically, and on the hidden test several hardware-sensitivity instances are solved to proven optimality by every MILP run, so that experiment separates methods least (positive-control gain 1.2 points vs 1.4 points of seed noise).
